title: sqlparse.split doesn't split after BEGIN...END block containing DROP TABLE IF EXISTS
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

A `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ...` inside a BEGIN ... END block makes the splitter treat that IF as control-flow IF, so the block never closes and the following statement is glued on.

```python
import sqlparse
sql = """CREATE TASK t1 AS
BEGIN
    CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE temp1;
    DROP TABLE IF EXISTS temp1;
END;
EXECUTE TASK t1;"""
print(len(sqlparse.split(sql)))
```

Expected: 2 statements; the first is the CREATE TASK ... END; and the second is `EXECUTE TASK t1;`.
Actual: 1 statement (everything in one string).

In general, `IF EXISTS` / `IF NOT EXISTS` should not be treated as an IF control-flow construct when splitting, wherever it appears. Plain top-level `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS FOO;\n\nSELECT * FROM BAR;` must keep splitting into 2 statements.
acceptance: The example above splits into exactly 2 statements, with CREATE TASK in the first and EXECUTE TASK in the second
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS foo; SELECT 1; still splits into 2 statements
